title: Setting Up a Database in Spring Boot
description: Add dependencies, configure H2 or MySQL, and verify the connection.

slides.title: Add the Required Dependencies 🛠️
slides.content:
# Spring Data JPA Starter

In your `pom.xml`, add:

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

And a database driver. For **H2** (in‑memory, great for development):

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
    <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
    <scope>runtime</scope>
</dependency>
```

For **MySQL** (production), you'd add the MySQL connector.

quizData.question: Which starter should you include to use Spring Data JPA?
quizData.explanation: spring‑boot‑starter‑data‑jpa brings in JPA, Hibernate, and Spring Data JPA.

slides.title: Configure application.properties
slides.content: Add these properties to configure the database connection and JPA behavior:
slides.codeSnippet:
# H2 in‑memory database
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
spring.datasource.driverClassName=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=

# JPA
spring.jpa.database-platform=org.hibernate.dialect.H2Dialect
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.jpa.show-sql=true

# H2 console (optional)
spring.h2.console.enabled=true

slides.title: What `ddl-auto` Means 📖
slides.content:
# Schema Generation Options

* `ddl-auto=update` – automatically creates/updates tables based on your entities (good for development).
* `ddl-auto=create` – drops and recreates tables each time.
* `ddl-auto=create-drop` – creates tables, then drops them when the application stops.
* `ddl-auto=validate` – only validates that the schema matches entities, does not change it.

**Never use `update` or `create` in production** – use a migration tool like Flyway or Liquibase instead.

slides.title: H2 Console 🖥️
slides.content: With `spring.h2.console.enabled=true`, you can access the H2 web console at `http://localhost:8080/h2-console`. Use JDBC URL `jdbc:h2:mem:testdb` to see your tables.
